description: The bar chart illustrates the number of participants who selected each of seven evaluation criteria when assessing a generative-AI-driven claim retrieval system, as described in the paper “A Generative-AI-Driven Claim Retrieval System Capable of Detecting and Retrieving Claims from Social Media Platforms in Multiple Languages.” The vertical axis lists the criteria in descending order of participant selection: “Relevant FCs” (6 participants), “FC Summary” (5), “Relevance Explanation” (3), “Clarity and Simplicity” (3), “Overall Summary” (2), “Filters” (1), and “Veracity Explanation” (1). The horizontal axis, labeled “Number of Participants,” ranges from 0 to 6 with tick marks at intervals of 2. Each criterion is represented by a horizontal bar of distinct color—ranging from dark purple for “Relevant FCs” to light green for “Veracity Explanation”—with the exact count labeled at the end of each bar. The chart visually emphasizes that “Relevant FCs” was the most frequently selected criterion, while “Filters” and “Veracity Explanation” were the least selected, each chosen by only one participant. No grouping or stacking is present; bars are sorted in descending order by participant count, and no additional annotations or emphasis (e.g., shading or bolding) are applied beyond the color coding and numerical labels.
